args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money per FIN-212

src/money.py documented banker's rounding per FIN-212 but quantize was
using ROUND_HALF_UP, causing test_half_even to fail in the nightly
build. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so ties are rounded to the even cent.

args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (0.5 cents ties round to the even cent, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was computing with `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite the docstring claiming `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Change
- `src/money.py`: switch `quantize(rounding=...)` from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, matching the documented behavior and FIN-212.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch (commit `08d3cd5986`) passed, including `test_half_even` (e.g. `2.675 -> 2.68`, `2.665 -> 2.66`).

Reviewers: @alex
args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Diagnosis**: `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `quantize` even though the docstring (and FIN-212) specified banker's rounding, which is why `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` failed in the nightly build.
- **Fix**: Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and changed the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` so half-cent ties round to the even cent (e.g. `2.675 → 2.68`, `2.665 → 2.66`).
- **CI**: Ran CI on the branch (run `ci-0001`) — it **passed**.
- **PR**: Opened PR #101 against `main` requesting review from **alex**: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

No changes were pushed to `main` directly; merging awaits alex's/code-owner approval as per policy.
